questions.prompt: Why does Google say to set minimum acceptable levels before testing?

options.text: So that the test can be finished faster, with fewer prompts to run
options.explanation: The level is a bar for judging the results. It does not shorten the test.

options.text: So that the vendor can approve the launch on behalf of the studio
options.explanation: The vendor does not approve launches. The studio decides.

options.text: So you can judge the results against an expectation set in advance
options.explanation: Right. Google says to think about minimum levels before testing, so that results can be evaluated against them.

questions.prompt: What does OpenAI say a human reviewer needs?

options.text: Only the final output, so that the review is not influenced by the source
options.explanation: OpenAI says the reviewer should have the original information, so the output can be checked.

options.text: Easy access to the information needed to check the output, such as the notes
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says humans should have access to any information needed to verify the outputs.

options.text: A score from the model, so that the reviewer can simply agree with it
options.explanation: OpenAI recommends human review of the output, not a human who repeats a model's score.

questions.prompt: Google says some tasks often pose a lower risk. Which one?

options.text: Long content that goes out with no review at all
options.explanation: Google names greater human oversight as lower risk, not less review.

options.text: Short content that a person reviews before it is used
options.explanation: Right. Google says tasks with greater human oversight, such as short-form content reviewed by a human, often pose a lower risk.

options.text: Any content, as long as the average test score is high
options.explanation: Google suggests focusing on worst-case performance, not the average.
